memory_update.text: Add AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC as direct US-listed semiconductor equipment candidates for the leading_edge_foundry_and_semi_equipment node; these were not in the seed universe but are central to wafer-fab/process-control exposure.
TSM and ASML remain the cleanest public-market mappings for leading-edge foundry capacity and lithography bottlenecks, respectively.

AMAT offers broad equipment exposure across materials engineering, deposition, etch, CMP, metrology/inspection, wafer packaging, and implant; this breadth makes it less pure than ASML but highly relevant.

Potential second-tier or adjacent US-listed names not included due to candidate limit: TER for test automation, AEIS for power delivery into semiconductor tools, COHU for test/inspection, FORM for probe cards, and ACLS for ion implantation. These require a separate less-obvious-suppliers pass.

Direct AI-chip customers such as NVDA, AMD, AVGO, AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, and META are exposed to the node as buyers of leading-edge foundry capacity, but this pass prioritized asset owners and equipment leaders rather than downstream customers.
For leading-edge foundry and semiconductor equipment, keep TSM and ASML as anchor names because they map directly to wafer capacity and EUV lithography scarcity.
Add AMAT, LRCX and KLAC as core US-listed WFE/process-control candidates tied to AI-driven leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM and advanced packaging investment.

Potential second-order suppliers not included due to the 5-candidate cap: TER for AI/HBM test, FORM for probe cards and test subsystems, MKSI for vacuum/photonics/laser/precision subsystems, AEIS for power subsystems, and ENTG for specialty materials/filtration. These should be checked in a follow-up supplier-components pass.

Current evidence suggests the node is real but may bifurcate: near-term AI scarcity appears concentrated in advanced packaging/HBM, while WFE/lithography/process-control governs the medium-term rate of supply expansion.

AMAT, LRCX and KLAC are core US-listed equipment/process-control leaders for leading-edge foundry capacity expansion; they should remain in the node universe even if near-term AI scarcity centers on HBM and packaging.

ONTO and VECO are less-obvious US-listed equipment beneficiaries with direct exposure to advanced-node metrology, HBM, EUV-adjacent processes and advanced packaging; both merit follow-up evidence checks on revenue mix and customer concentration.

Test and probe-card names such as TER and FORM were not included in the five-candidate cap but should be expanded in a separate adjacent chokepoint pass focused on known-good-die, wafer probe, system-level test, HBM test and chiplet/CoW validation.

For this node, the highest-value falsification data are tool lead times, customer capex pull-ins or cancellations, cleanroom constraints, tool-of-record wins, export-control impact, advanced-packaging order durability, and foundry/logic versus memory utilization.
